title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 22 (Contract caused by mistake of one party as to matter of fact)

content.overview: Section 22 provides that a contract is not voidable merely because it was caused by one of the parties to it being under a mistake as to a matter of fact.
content.glance: Unilateral mistake of fact does not by itself make the contract voidable.
content.study: A contract is not voidable merely because one party was under a mistake as to a matter of fact. Bilateral essential fact mistake is under s. 20 (void). Unilateral mistake may still interact with fraud or misrepresentation if the other party caused the mistake. Current-law framing: confirm the mistake is unilateral as to fact; apply s. 22’s non-voidability rule; check for fraud/misrepresentation or bilateral mistake.

sections.heading: Unilateral mistake of fact
sections.body: Contract not voidable merely because caused by one party’s mistake as to a matter of fact.

provisions.title: Contract caused by mistake of one party as to matter of fact

examples.title: One-sided factual error
examples.body: A alone is mistaken about a fact. Absent fraud or misrepresentation, the contract is not voidable merely on that ground under s. 22.

hypotheticals.question: Can unilateral mistake ever affect the contract?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not under s. 22 alone; but fraud, misrepresentation, or bilateral essential fact mistake may still apply under other sections.

misconceptions.trap: Any factual mistake by one party voids the contract.
misconceptions.correction: Section 22: unilateral mistake of fact does not by itself make the contract voidable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 22 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm unilateral mistake of fact. II. Apply non-voidability. III. Check fraud/misrepresentation or s. 20. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Contrast with bilateral mistake under s. 20.
